data.dialogue: SRE Lead: Our FastAPI risk prediction container on AWS EC2 returned HTTP 500 during blue-green rollout. ML Engineer: I checked the CloudWatch traceback. Joblib failed to unpickle RiskDomainFeatureGenerator because the custom transformer was defined in __main__ instead of the installed src package. SRE Lead: How did we fix it? ML Engineer: We moved RiskDomainFeatureGenerator into src.risk_predictor.components.data_transformation and installed the package with pip install -e . before retraining.
data.summary: FastAPI container failed with HTTP 500 due to a joblib __main__ unpickling error. Moving RiskDomainFeatureGenerator into the installable src package resolved the issue.

data.dialogue: Researcher: Full fine-tuning of our 7B parameter transformer ran out of GPU VRAM on a single 24GB A10G. Tech Lead: Switch to QLoRA with 4-bit NormalFloat quantization and attach rank-8 LoRA adapters to the query and value projections. Researcher: I ran the experiment with r=8 and lora_alpha=16. Trainable parameters dropped below 0.5% and ROUGE-L improved by 14.2%.
data.summary: Full 7B fine-tuning exceeded 24GB VRAM. Switching to 4-bit QLoRA (r=8, alpha=16 on query/value projections) reduced trainable parameters below 0.5% and increased ROUGE-L by 14.2%.

data.dialogue: Data Engineer: The nightly Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift job flagged a p-value of 0.003 on the BMI feature in production traffic. MLOps Engineer: Let's inspect drift_report.yaml. Since p < 0.05, covariate shift is confirmed. Data Engineer: I triggered the automated retraining webhook on GitHub Actions and registered version 2 of the model in DagsHub MLflow.
data.summary: Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift detection flagged covariate shift on BMI (p=0.003 < 0.05), triggering automated retraining and registering model version 2 in DagsHub MLflow.

data.dialogue: AI Engineer: Naive dense vector search in Qdrant missed exact error codes like ERR_CUDA_OOM_404 in user queries. Architect: Dense embeddings struggle with rare alphanumeric identifiers. Combine Qdrant cosine similarity with BM25 lexical search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion. AI Engineer: Added Hybrid RRF plus cross-feature re-ranking. Recall@3 jumped from 0.67 to 1.00.
data.summary: Naive dense vector search missed exact alphanumeric error codes. Combining Qdrant dense search with BM25 via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and re-ranking increased Recall@3 from 0.67 to 1.00.

data.dialogue: CV Engineer: Our ResNet-18 poultry disease classifier Docker image was 2.6GB because pip pulled CUDA wheels on Linux. DevOps Lead: Add --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu to requirements.txt and apply dynamic INT8 quantization. CV Engineer: Done. Image size shrank by 82% and validation accuracy remained at 100% across all four pathology classes.
data.summary: Using CPU PyTorch wheels and dynamic INT8 quantization reduced the ResNet-18 Docker image size by 82% while maintaining 100% validation accuracy across four pathology classes.

data.dialogue: ML Engineer: Teammates are re-running data ingestion and base model preparation on every commit even when only evaluation code changed. Platform Lead: Define a four-stage DAG in dvc.yaml tracking deps, params, outs, and scores.json metrics. ML Engineer: Now dvc repro checks SHA256 hashes in dvc.lock and skips unchanged upstream stages automatically.
data.summary: Defining a four-stage DAG in dvc.yaml with dvc.lock hash tracking allowed dvc repro to skip unchanged upstream stages and track scores.json metrics reproducibly.

data.dialogue: Product Manager: How do we detect when the RAG assistant hallucinates facts not present in the retrieved Qdrant chunks? LLMOps Engineer: We added an automated faithfulness monitor that computes lexical and n-gram grounding overlap between the generated answer and retrieved context chunks. Product Manager: Great, alert the on-call channel whenever faithfulness drops below 0.50.
data.summary: An automated LLM faithfulness monitor computes grounding overlap between generated answers and retrieved Qdrant chunks, triggering alerts when faithfulness falls below 0.50.

data.dialogue: Cloud Architect: Compare our AWS EC2 deployment against Azure Web App for Containers for the vision service. DevOps Engineer: AWS EC2 provides full VM control via a self-hosted GitHub runner and ECR, whereas Azure Web App offers managed PaaS container hosting with automatic HTTPS termination. Cloud Architect: Keep both deployment jobs in .github/workflows/main.yaml for multi-cloud redundancy.
data.summary: AWS EC2 uses a self-hosted runner for IaaS control while Azure Web App provides managed PaaS container hosting; both are maintained in GitHub Actions for multi-cloud redundancy.
